why: the named falsifier: a voice-identical clip re-baked by a DIFFERENT engine that reuses the old content hash, and a clip whose measured loudness sits a whole voice-average away from the declared target

sameVoiceDifferentEngine.note: everything a reader can see is identical: same character, same voice spec, same line, same bitrate. Only the synthesiser changed.

samePinDifferentRelease.note: a weights release moves every style vector; the voice id does not change

driftedClip.note: -19.6 is the voice average EC-PACK-52 measured against a sound bank mastered at -16

mustNotBe: the re-baked clip keeping the old clip id, so its file name, its manifest row and its sha256 all still look current while the audio behind them is a different synthesiser; or a bake reporting green for a clip measured outside the declared tolerance; or a bank whose loudness was asserted on the PCM that went into the encoder rather than on the decoded Opus file that shipped
